1 1.
This application under Section 24 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908 is at the instance of wife praying for transfer of Matrimonial Suit No.3216 of 2021 pending before the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court at Alipore.
2.

entities.text: Moumita Dey Sarkar vs Subrata Dey Sarkar on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Additional District Judge, 3rd Court at Alipore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The marriage between the parties took place on September 22, 2012.
Thereafter, the petitioner and the opposite party started living together as wife and husband and a female child was born out of the wedlock on October 17, 2016.
The petitioner/wife left her matrimonial home on June 1, 2021.

3. The petitioner claims that she is at present residing at Mainaguri and the distance between Mainaguri and the Court at Alipore is about 636 kilometers and it takes around 13 hours to travel one way to reach Alipore from the present residence of the petitioner.
The petitioner states the minor daughter of the petitioner is at present aged about 9 years.
4. Learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that it is difficult for the petitioner to travel from Mainaguri to Alipore to proceed with the matrimonial suit.
That apart, it is also difficult for the petitioner to come to Kolkata leaving her minor daughter alone in the house.

5. Learned advocate appearing for the petitioner places reliance upon a decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajani Kishor Pardeshi vs. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi reported in (2005)
12 SCC 237 in support of his contention that the convenience of the wife is to be preferred over the convenience of the husband while deciding an application for transfer of a suit/proceeding.
6.

entities.text:
Rajani Kishor Pardeshi vs. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi reported in (2005)
12 SCC 237
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra Mr. Samanta, learned advocate for the opposite party submits that apart from the matrimonial suit the petitioner has instituted several criminal proceedings under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, under Section 125 of the Criminal Procedure Code and under the provisions of the Domestic Violence Act and all are pending before the Alipore Court.

He then submits that since all other proceedings are pending before the Alipore Court the instant application for transfer is liable to be rejected in view of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Soma Chowdhury vs. Gourab Chowdhury reported in (2004) 13 SCC 462.

entities.text: Soma Chowdhury vs. Gourab Chowdhury reported in (2004) 13 SCC 462
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Samanta places reliance on the disability certificate issued by the authority of the District Hospital at Jalpaiguri in support of his claim the opposite party is a person suffering from 50% permanent disability and, therefore, it is not possible for the petitioner to travel to Jalpaiguri for contesting the matrimonial suit as prayed for by the petitioner in the application for transfer.

7. Heard the learned advocates for the parties and perused the materials placed.
8.

There is no quarrel to the proposition of law laid down in Rajani Kishore Pardeshi (supra) that while deciding an application for transfer of a suit or proceeding, convenience of the wife is to be preferred over the convenience of the husband.

However, after hearing the learned advocates for the respective parties and after going through the materials placed on record, this Court is inclined to take a slightly different view taking note of the special facts and circumstances of this case.

Smt. Moumita Dey Sarkar vs Subrata Dey Sarkar on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111003233/
2 9.

entities.text: Moumita Dey Sarkar vs Subrata Dey Sarkar on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner claims to have left the matrimonial home in the month of June 2021.

Immediately thereafter, the petitioner lodged a proceeding being ACGR Case No.2620 of 2021 corresponding to Kasba PS Case No.194 of 2021 and the same is pending before the Court of the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate at Alipore.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate at Alipore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Thereafter, the petitioner filed an application under Section 125 of the Criminal Procedure Code sometimes in the month of October 2021 which was registered as Maintenance Case No.760 of 2021.
The maintenance case is pending before the learned 6th Judicial Magistrate at Alipore.
The petitioner filed the instant matrimonial suit on November 11, 2021 before the learned District Judge at Alipore.
The matrimonial suit was subsequently transferred to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court at Alipore and the same is at present pending before that Court.

entities.text: Additional District Judge, 6th Court at Alipore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Even after filing the matrimonial suit the petitioner filed a proceeding under the provisions of Domestic Violence Act which was registered as Misc. Case No.438 of 2022,
which is pending before the learned Additional District Judge at Alipore.
10.
Thus, from the aforesaid undisputed facts it appears that the petitioner/wife instituted all the proceedings prior to and after filing of the matrimonial suit before Alipore Court.

If the petitioner could file four proceedings before Alipore Court after she left her matrimonial suit and while she was residing at Mainaguri in the district of Jalpaiguri, this Court is not inclined to accept the contention of the petitioner that it is difficult for the petitioner to come to Alipore Court to proceed with the matrimonial suit.
It is not in dispute that the petitioner is also pursuing other proceedings in accordance with law before the Courts at Alipore.
That apart, the matrimonial suit has proceeded to the stage of evidence.
The learned advocate for the petitioner submits that examination-in-chief by way of an affidavit has already been filed and December 19, 2024 has been fixed for evidence.

11. In Soma Chowdhury (supra) the Hon'ble Supreme Court after taking note of the fact that the proceedings under the Criminal Procedure Code was pending before the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Alipore transferred the matrimonial proceeding pending before the Court of the District Judge, South Tripura, Udaipur to a Court at Alipore.

entities.text: Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Alipore
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Court of the District Judge, South Tripura, Udaipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Though the application for transfer in Soma Chowdhury (supra) was at the instance of the wife but this Court cannot lose sight of the fact that the Hon'ble Supreme Court transferred the matrimonial proceeding between the contesting parties to the place where the criminal proceeding at the instance of the wife is pending.

12. Taking note of the fact that other proceedings at the instance of the wife are pending at Alipore and the wife is still pursing those proceedings at Alipore, this Court is not inclined to allow the prayer for transfer.

13. Since the date has been fixed for evidence, a request is made to the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court at Alipore to fix consecutive dates for evidence of the wife and the opposite party shall be obliged to bear the travel expenses of the petitioner/wife on all occasions she has to appear in the Matrimonial Suit as well as reasonable expenses for temporary stay of the petitioner in connection thereto.

entities.text: Additional District Judge, 3rd Court at Alipore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The aforesaid payment should be made upon production of documents in support thereof.

14. With the above observation and directions civil order stands disposed of.
